CADCraft design system

Components

  • Button (.md): The one button: it runs the action its label names, on Cursor's measured .cursor-button recipe.
  • Card (.md): A raised block that groups related controls on an inset surface.
  • Chip (.md): A small pill for a count or a status word, on Cursor's measured .monaco-count-badge recipe.
  • Field (.md): The one single-line text field: it edits a string and shows a hint while the string is empty.
  • Icon button (.md): The icon-only control: a square target that draws a code-drawn glyph and names itself with a tooltip.
  • Row (.md): A list row: the full-width clickable band that carries one entry of a list, menu or pane.
  • Section label (.md): A quiet heading that names the block of controls under it.

Rules

  • Rules (.md): every trap and rule ID, the page that answers it and the check that enforces it

Check command: cargo xtask system-check. Machine index: llms.txt.

Button

Description

The one button: it runs the action its label names, on Cursor's measured .cursor-button recipe.

source crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-clone, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the recipe is measured from Cursor's CSS into theme.rs constants, and no registry item ships it.

Examples

Default: a primary button in a dialog footer.

Real uses, 0 call sites (rg 'widgets::button' crates/ui-egui/src): the canonical entry lands first; the pilot and safe-moves steps move the surfaces onto it.

Example: A primary button in a dialog footer. (docs/system/examples/button/default.rs)

// The dialog owns the layout; the widget owns the chrome.
if widgets::button(ui, "Save", widgets::Kind::Primary).clicked() {
    save();
}

Example: A ghost button beside an icon button on the tool bar. (docs/system/examples/button/in-toolbar.rs)

if widgets::button(ui, "Publish", widgets::Kind::Ghost).clicked() {
    publish();
}
if widgets::icon_button(ui, icons::Icon::Share, 26.0, "Share", false).clicked() {
    share();
}

Variants

Kind

  • Ghost: the transparent fill with a hairline border, for tool bars and quiet actions. Used at 0 call sites.
  • Primary: the action fill, for the dialog's main action. Used at 0 call sites.
  • Danger: the error fill, for destructive actions. Used at 0 call sites.

Example: The ghost kind, a quiet action on a tool bar. (docs/system/examples/button/kind-ghost.rs)

if widgets::button(ui, "Manage", widgets::Kind::Ghost).clicked() {
    open_manage();
}

Example: The primary kind, the dialog's action. (docs/system/examples/button/kind-primary.rs)

if widgets::button(ui, "Create", widgets::Kind::Primary).clicked() {
    create();
}

Example: The danger kind, a destructive action. (docs/system/examples/button/kind-danger.rs)

if widgets::button(ui, "Delete", widgets::Kind::Danger).clicked() {
    delete();
}

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestNothing is over the button.Click it.Ghost shows its hairline border.by hand
HoverThe pointer is over it.Click it.Ghost gains a fill and a brighter border; the filled kinds drop to 0.8 opacity.by hand
PressedThe pointer is held down on it.Release to click.The same fill as hover.by hand
FocusedKeyboard focus arrives by Tab.Enter or Space clicks it.A 1px ring just inside the 2px radius.by hand
DisabledThe caller's condition is false.Nothing.The fill, border and label at 0.5 opacity.by hand

State precedence

  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the button; hover only changes the fill.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled button keeps its rest colours under the pointer and takes no click.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion — the recipes paint each state directly, and the app's Animation preference governs egui's own widgets.

Props

Signature: pub fn button(ui: &mut egui::Ui, label: &str, kind: Kind) -> egui::Response.

  • label: the action's text; the widget translates it and draws it at 14px.
  • kind: Kind::Ghost, Kind::Primary or Kind::Danger.

Usage

When to use

  • The user runs one action and expects it to happen now.

When not to use

  • The control is an icon with no label. Use icon_button instead.
  • The text is a status rather than an action. Use chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/button-recipe: When a button is drawn, use RADIUS_CONTROL (2px), BUTTON_PAD_X (8px), BUTTON_PAD_Y (4px) and FONT_BUTTON (14px), because .cursor-button measures border-radius:2px; font-size:14px; gap:4px; padding:4px 8px and the app's 6/8/10/12 scale came from a third-party clone. Evidence: measured 2px radius, 4px 8px padding and 14px type, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §3. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: rect_filled(rect, 6.0, fill) on a hand-painted button.
  • Do: button(ui, "Save", Kind::Primary) and let the recipe fill it.
  • rule/button-states: When a button is hovered, pressed or disabled, use HOVER_OPACITY (0.8) and DISABLED_OPACITY (0.5), because .cursor-button-primary-clickable:not(.disabled):hover is opacity:.8 and .cursor-button-primary.disabled is opacity:.5. Evidence: measured 0.8 and 0.5, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §3. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: paint the hover fill at control_hover*0.6 by hand.
  • Do: call button and let the hover opacity come from HOVER_OPACITY.
  • rule/button-focus: When a button has keyboard focus, paint the FOCUS_OUTLINE_W (1px) ring at FOCUS_OUTLINE_OFFSET (-1), because .cursor-button.tab-focusable:focus is outline:1px solid var(--vscode-focusBorder); outline-offset:-1px. Evidence: measured 1px and -1px, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §3. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: leave a focused button with no visible ring.
  • Do: paint the ring just inside the 2px radius so the corners stay followed.

Content

  • Not applicable: the label comes from the caller; the widget draws it verbatim.

Anti-slop

  • rule/button-canonical: When a surface needs a button, call button rather than painting a fill, because the inventory counted 3 hand-painted ghost buttons with 3 radii and 3 hover fills. Evidence: app 3/3 ghost buttons, .design-system/boss/triage/inventory.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: ui.add(egui::Button::new(text).fill(t.accent).min_size(vec2(84.0, 22.0))) in a surface.
  • Do: button(ui, "Save", Kind::Primary).

Limits

  • Not applicable: no count or length limit; the label sizes the button and the caller shortens it.

Accessibility

Rests on the painted rect with Sense::click(), whose widget info gives egui a button node named by the label.

Props

Signature: pub fn card<R>(ui: &mut egui::Ui, add: impl FnOnce(&mut egui::Ui) -> R) -> egui::InnerResponse<R>.

  • add: builds the card's content; the card owns the fill, the border, the radius and the padding.

Usage

When to use

  • Related controls need their own surface: settings, a summary, an inline detail block.

When not to use

  • The content is one control. Use field or row directly instead.
  • The block floats over the drawing and needs a title. Use the app's dialog (crate::modal) instead.

Rules

  • rule/card-recipe: When a card is drawn, use RADIUS_CARD (4px), a HAIRLINE (1px) border and CARD_PADDING (16px), because .composer-history-pane measures border:1px solid; border-radius:4px and cards pad at the 16px rung. Evidence: measured 4px radius and 16px padding, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §1.17. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: a card at radius 8 with a drop shadow.
  • Do: card(ui, |ui| { ... }) and let the recipe draw the frame.

Content

  • Not applicable: the card's content is the caller's.

Anti-slop

  • rule/card-canonical: When a surface needs a grouped block, call card rather than a bare Frame, because the inventory counted assistant cards at radius 6 and 8 while the composer's frame paints 8 — one radius where there could be two. Evidence: app 3/3 card radii, .design-system/boss/triage/inventory.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: egui::Frame::new().fill(t.field).corner_radius(8.0).show(ui, ...) in a surface.
  • Do: card(ui, |ui| { ... }).

Limits

  • Not applicable: no count or size limit; the card grows with its content.

Accessibility

Rests on the caller's content; the card is a painted frame with no role of its own.

Props

Signature: pub fn chip(ui: &mut egui::Ui, text: &str, kind: ChipKind) -> egui::Response.

  • text: the count or the status word; the widget translates it and draws it at 11px.
  • kind: ChipKind::Neutral, ChipKind::Accent or ChipKind::Danger.

Usage

When to use

  • A count, a state or a short status needs to sit beside a label or a row.

When not to use

  • The text runs a sentence. Use section_label instead.
  • The text is an action the user runs. Use button instead.

Rules

  • rule/chip-recipe: When a chip is drawn, use RADIUS_PILL (11px), CHIP_PAD_X (6px), CHIP_PAD_Y (3px) and FONT_CHIP (11px), because .monaco-count-badge measures border-radius:11px; font-size:11px; line-height:11px; padding:3px 6px with an 18px floor. Evidence: measured 11px radius, 3px 6px padding and 18px floor, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §7. Check: test crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: a 3px-radius box with theme::small() text as a count.
  • Do: chip(ui, "3", ChipKind::Neutral).
  • rule/chip-kinds: When a chip carries the action or error status, use the accent or error fill with on_accent text, because .cursor-badge's variants fill from button.background, badge.background and errorForeground with their own foreground. Evidence: measured 3 fills, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §7. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: rect_filled(rect, 2.0, t.warn) for a quiet count.
  • Do: pass ChipKind::Accent and let the widget fill from Tokens::accent.

Content

  • Not applicable: the text is the caller's; the widget draws it verbatim.

Anti-slop

  • rule/chip-canonical: When a surface needs a pill, call chip rather than painting one, because the inventory counted the same chip at radius 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8. Evidence: app 5/5 chip radii, .design-system/boss/triage/inventory.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: rect_filled(r, 3.0, hover ? t.control_hover : t.control) beside a label.
  • Do: chip(ui, "M", ChipKind::Neutral).

Limits

  • Not applicable: no count or length limit; the caller keeps the text to a word or a count.

Accessibility

Rests on the painted rect with Sense::click(), whose widget info gives egui a button node named by the text.

Props

Signature: pub fn field(ui: &mut egui::Ui, text: &mut String, hint: &str) -> egui::Response.

  • text: the buffer the field edits in place.
  • hint: shown in the placeholder colour while text is empty.

Usage

When to use

  • The user types one line of text: a name, a path, a value.

When not to use

  • The text runs over several lines. Use egui::TextEdit::multiline in the surface instead.
  • The user picks one of a known set. Use row in a menu instead.

Rules

  • rule/field-recipe: When a field is drawn, use RADIUS_CONTROL (2px), FIELD_PAD_X (6px), FIELD_PAD_Y (4px) and CONTROL_H_INPUT (24px), because .monaco-inputbox measures border-radius:2px with inner padding:4px 6px and the view-pane filter input is 24px high. Evidence: measured 2px radius, 4px 6px padding and 24px height, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §4. Check: test crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: a stock TextEdit at egui's 6px widget radius.
  • Do: field(ui, &mut name, "Name").
  • rule/field-placeholder: When a field is empty, show its hint in text_faint, because Cursor paints input::placeholder with input.placeholderForeground. Evidence: measured 1 colour, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: a hint in full-strength text that reads as a value.
  • Do: let field paint the hint at Tokens::text_faint.
  • rule/field-focus: When a field has focus, paint the FOCUS_OUTLINE_W (1px) ring at FOCUS_OUTLINE_OFFSET (-1), because .monaco-inputbox's focus is outline:1px solid; outline-offset:-1px. Evidence: measured 1px and -1px, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: a glow or a 2px border as the focus cue.
  • Do: the 1px accent ring following the 2px radius.

Content

  • Not applicable: the hint comes from the caller; the widget draws it verbatim.

Anti-slop

  • rule/field-canonical: When a surface needs a text field, call field rather than adding a stock TextEdit, because the inventory counted 4 heights and 3 fills for "a place you type". Evidence: app 4/4 field heights, .design-system/boss/triage/inventory.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut v).desired_width(f32::INFINITY)) in a surface.
  • Do: field(ui, &mut v, "Name").

Limits

  • Not applicable: no count or length limit; the caller validates what it needs.

Accessibility

Rests on egui's TextEdit, which gives accesskit a text edit node, inside the painted frame.

Props

Signature: pub fn icon_button(ui: &mut egui::Ui, icon: Icon, size: f32, tooltip: &str, selected: bool) -> egui::Response.

  • icon: the icons::Icon variant; the glyph is drawn by icons::paint.
  • size: the square target in points, which the surface picks from its own ladder.
  • tooltip: the control's name; it is the accesskit name and the hover text.
  • selected: the on/off fill for view toggles.

Usage

When to use

  • An action is understood as a glyph (Save, Undo, Close) and the surface has no room for a label.

When not to use

  • The action's meaning needs words. Use button instead.
  • The control shows a status rather than running an action. Use chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/icon-button-recipe: When an icon-only control is drawn, use a square target at RADIUS_CARD (4px), because .composer-bar-button measures border-radius:4px and the estate paints its icon buttons at 1, 3 and 6px today. Evidence: measured 4px, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §1.5. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: rect_filled(rect, 6.0, ...) under a toolbar glyph.
  • Do: icon_button(ui, Icon::Save, 26.0, "Save", false).
  • rule/icon-button-states: When an icon button is hovered or selected, fill with control_hover or select_bg, because .composer-bar-button hovers at toolbar.hoverBackground and a selected row uses list.activeSelectionBackground. Evidence: measured 2 fills, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §1.5. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: paint control_hover*0.6 by hand.
  • Do: pass selected and let icon_button choose the fill.
  • rule/icon-button-name: When an icon-only control is drawn, pass a tooltip, because an icon carries no text and every Cursor icon button names itself on hover. Evidence: principle wcag: 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §1.5. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: icon_button(ui, Icon::Close, 14.0, "", false).
  • Do: icon_button(ui, Icon::Close, 14.0, "Close", false).

Content

  • Not applicable: the name is the tooltip argument; the widget never invents copy.

Anti-slop

  • rule/icon-button-canonical: When a surface needs an icon-only control, call icon_button rather than painting a fill under icons::paint, because the inventory counted 4 sizes and 4 hover treatments for the same control. Evidence: app 4/4 icon buttons, .design-system/boss/triage/inventory.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: ui.interact(...) then painter.rect_filled(rect, 3.0, ...) under a glyph.
  • Do: icon_button(ui, Icon::Close, 14.0, "Close", false).

Limits

  • Not applicable: no count or length limit; size is the caller's.

Accessibility

Rests on the painted rect with Sense::click(), whose widget info gives egui a button node named by the tooltip.

Row

Description

A list row: the full-width clickable band that carries one entry of a list, menu or pane.

source crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/list-dead-gap, trap/control-height, trap/hover-beats-focus.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the recipe is measured from Cursor's CSS into theme.rs constants; no registry item ships it.

Examples

Default: a row in a list.

Real uses, 0 call sites (rg 'widgets::row' crates/ui-egui/src): the canonical entry lands first; the pilot and safe-moves steps move the surfaces onto it.

Example files

Example: A row in a list, with its content painted into the rect. (docs/system/examples/row/default.rs)

let r = widgets::row(ui, false);
ui.painter().text(r.rect.left_center() + vec2(6.0, 0.0), egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER, name, theme::body(), t.text);

Example: A selected row inside a card. (docs/system/examples/row/in-card.rs)

widgets::card(ui, |ui| {
    let r = widgets::row(ui, selected);
    ui.painter().text(r.rect.left_center() + vec2(6.0, 0.0), egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER, name, theme::body(), t.text);
});

Variants

Not applicable: single signature

One row chrome; selected is a state and the content is the caller's.

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestNothing is over the row.Click it.Nothing; the caller's content shows.by hand
HoverThe pointer is over it.Click it.A control_hover fill at the 4px radius.by hand
Selectedselected is true.Click it, or click another row.A select_bg fill that outranks hover.by hand
FocusedKeyboard focus arrives by Tab.Enter or Space clicks it.A 1px ring just inside the 4px radius.by hand

State precedence

  • Hover and Selected: Selected wins. A selected row keeps the selection fill under the pointer.
  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the row.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion — the recipes paint each state directly, and the app's Animation preference governs egui's own widgets.

Props

Signature: pub fn row(ui: &mut egui::Ui, selected: bool) -> egui::Response.

  • selected: the selection fill for the active entry; the caller paints the row's content into the returned response's rect and names it.

Usage

When to use

  • A list, a menu or a pane shows one entry per line and the whole line is the hit area.

When not to use

  • The line runs one labelled action. Use button instead.
  • The line is a status word. Use chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/row-recipe: When a list row is drawn, use CONTROL_H_ROW (22px) at RADIUS_CARD (4px), because .explorer-item measures height:22px; line-height:22px and .action-menu-item measures border-radius:4px. Evidence: measured 22px height and 4px radius, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §2. Check: test crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: rows at 20px and 26px in the same list.
  • Do: row(ui, selected) and paint the content into its rect.
  • rule/row-states: When a row is hovered or selected, fill with control_hover or select_bg, because .sidebar-list-item hovers list.hoverBackground and selects list.inactiveSelectionBackground. Evidence: measured 2 fills, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §2. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: paint control_hover*0.5 by hand.
  • Do: pass selected and let the row choose the fill.

Content

  • Not applicable: the row's content is the caller's.

Anti-slop

  • rule/row-canonical: When a list needs a row, call row rather than painting a fill, because the inventory counted rows at radius 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8 with five hover alphas. Evidence: app 5/5 row radii, .design-system/boss/triage/inventory.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: p.rect_filled(r, 2.0, if hovered { t.cmd_keyword_hover } else { t.list_row }) in a list.
  • Do: let r = row(ui, selected); then paint the content into r.rect.

Limits

  • Not applicable: no count or length limit; the list scrolls and the caller clips the text.

Accessibility

Rests on the painted rect with Sense::click(); the caller adds the widget info that names the row.

Section label

Description

A quiet heading that names the block of controls under it.

source crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/weight-shift.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the size and colour are measured from Cursor's CSS into theme.rs constants; no registry item ships it.

Examples

Default: a section label above a field.

Real uses, 0 call sites (rg 'widgets::section_label' crates/ui-egui/src): the canonical entry lands first; the pilot and safe-moves steps move the surfaces onto it.

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestAlways, once drawn.Read it.12px type in the placeholder colour, so it recedes under the content it names.by hand

State precedence

  • Not applicable: the label has one state; it never takes focus or hover.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion — the recipes paint each state directly, and the app's Animation preference governs egui's own widgets.

Props

Signature: pub fn section_label(ui: &mut egui::Ui, text: &str) -> egui::Response.

  • text: the label, written in sentence case (Model, Attach files).

Usage

When to use

  • A group of controls needs a name inside a card, a pane or a dialog.

When not to use

  • The text is an action. Use button instead.
  • The text is a value the user reads as content. Use a plain ui.label with Tokens::text instead.

Rules

  • rule/section-label-recipe: When a section label is drawn, use FONT_LABEL (12px) and text_faint, because .context-list-item and .picker-menu-item measure font-size:12px and Cursor paints its muted chrome text with input.placeholderForeground. Evidence: measured 12px, .design-system/cursor/recipes.md §9. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: a 14px bold label in full-strength text.
  • Do: section_label(ui, "Model").

Content

  • rule/section-label-sentence-case: When a section label is written, use sentence case with no trailing colon (Model, not MODEL:), because the label names a block and reads as a phrase rather than a shout. Evidence: principle platform: sentence-style capitalization for UI labels (Microsoft Writing Style Guide). Check: review docs/system/components/section-label.md.
  • Don't: "MODEL:"
  • Do: "Model"

Anti-slop

  • rule/section-label-canonical: When a surface needs a group name, call section_label rather than a bare proportional(14.0) label, because the inventory counted 3 section-header heights and fonts. Evidence: app 3/3 section headers, .design-system/boss/triage/inventory.md §4. Check: review crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs.
  • Don't: ui.label(RichText::new("Model").font(FontId::proportional(14.0))).
  • Do: section_label(ui, "Model").

Limits

  • Not applicable: no count or length limit; the caller keeps the label to a phrase.

Accessibility

Rests on egui's label; it is plain text with no role of its own.

What the check can't see

A reviewer or a browser covers these. Passing cargo xtask system-check says nothing about them.

  • the rendered result: contrast, optical size and spacing are not measured.
  • a control drawn by hand from tokens, with no literal left to see: the check reads values, not shapes.
  • a value that matches no token or constant today: the check freezes it in the ratchet, it does not bless it.
  • literals after a // on the same line, and code below a file's first mod tests.
  • files outside crates/ui-egui/src.
